definitions.explanation: the process of transferring responsibilities, work, or duties from one person to another

examples.japanese: {引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぎ{資料|しりょう}を{作成|さくせい}する。
{前任者|ぜんにんしゃ}からの{引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぎが{不十分|ふじゅうぶん}だった。
examples.english: The handover from my predecessor was insufficient.

examples.japanese: {退職|たいしょく}{前|まえ}に{引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぎを{完了|かんりょう}させなければならない。
examples.english: I need to complete the handover before I leave the company.

notes:
FORMATION:
{引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぐ (to take over, to succeed) → nominalized form

VERB FORM:
{引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぐ (godan) - to take over, to succeed to

RELATED COMPOUNDS:
- {引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぎ{書|しょ} (handover document)
- {引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぎ{資料|しりょう} (handover materials)
- {引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぎ{期間|きかん} (handover period)
- {業務|ぎょうむ}{引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぎ (work handover)

RELATED WORDS:
- {申|もう}し{送|おく}り (briefing, passing on information)
- {後任|こうにん} (successor)
- {前任|ぜんにん} (predecessor)

WORKPLACE USAGE:
Proper {引|ひ}き{継|つ}ぎ is considered essential in Japanese workplaces. Leaving without adequate handover is seen as irresponsible. Common when changing jobs, transferring departments, or retiring.
